Observed seq 0 (`_id: "AZ-lOaD-23Huse3YvZvx"` in .ds-logs-falco.alerts-default-2026.06.29-000007) and seq 1 (the 20:19–20:20 rule query) both return total 0 / returned 0 with truncated false, while seq 2 (20:00–21:00) returns total 3, all three being `falco.rule: "Adding ssh keys to authorized_keys"`, priority Warning, `fd.name: /root/.ssh/authorized_keys`, `proc.name: bash`, `proc.pname: containerd-shim`, `user.name: root`, `container.name: <NA>`, at 20:11:32.775, 20:14:11.072 and 20:17:30.874 — with identical `proc.cmdline` appending an `..._attacker attacker@elsewhere` key. Whether that rule fires at this rate routinely on soc-playground cannot be established here, and the only cross-window-varying field present (`falco.output_fields.container.id: a36492b5172b`) is listed as an unstable identifier and so could not evidence a delta anyway. A control run of the same `falco.rule` query over a live one-hour window a week back would have settled it.

l-002.evidence: The lead contains a single query, `change-mgmt.active-changes`, parameterized by host `soc-playground` and an instant `at: 2026-07-27T20:19:23Z` rather than a time range. The environment notes state explicitly that change-mgmt queries return a current change record set, carry no `@timestamp` bounds to move, and therefore have no control window or baseline-diff semantics. Consistent with that, `observed` seq 0 is an empty array and `baseline` is an empty list — not an empty control window but the absence of any baseline construct at all. The empty result means no CR record covers that host at that instant; it is a lookup answer, not a stream delta.
